rounds.text: IG P Petrochemicals Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 10.8x against a sector benchmark of 19.76x, and an EV/EBITDA of 5.54x versus its sector benchmark of 10.57x [E1, E6, E11]. Operational momentum has surged dramatically, evidenced by trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of 419% and quarterly operating margins expanding to 17% in September 2026 compared to 4% in the year-ago quarter [E21, E31]. The company demonstrates exceptional cash generation with a cash conversion of 51.00x for March 2026, backing reported profits entirely with operating cash flow of Rs 102 Cr [E34, E35]. Furthermore, a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21x combined with falling borrowings and a massive 79.8% drop in CWIP indicates that capital expenditure is largely complete and new capacity is primed to come online [E37, E39, E40]. Technical strength reinforces this fundamental value, with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and the price positioned above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50, E51]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over 3 years is -78% and the 3-year median ROE stands at a low 4% [E20, E28].

While recent trailing twelve-month figures show profit and margin recovery, the multi-year fundamental record reveals severe structural deterioration, highlighted by compounded profit growth of -28% over 10 years, -59% over 5 years, and -78% over 3 years [E18, E19, E20]. This historical destruction of earnings power is compounded by a poor 3-year sales growth rate of -6% and a poor 5-year sales growth rate of 11% [E16, E61]. Return profiles are equally concerning over medium timeframes, with a 3-year median ROE of just 4% and a last-year median ROE dropping to 0% [E28, E29, E68]. The valuation offers virtually no margin of safety at a thin 3.0% against the DCF intrinsic value [E46], leaving investors highly vulnerable given the stock sits near its 52-week high with an extreme annualised volatility of 55.4% and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -89.5% [E48, E54, E53]. Furthermore, free cash flow was negative at Rs -60 Cr in March 2026 [E36], and operating margins have an "Inconsistent" yearly trend over the last two years [E32]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E10, E21, E30, E31, E34, E35, E37, E39, E40, E45, E51, E52].

Conceded: [E18], [E19], [E20], [E16], [E28], [E29], [E36], [E53], [E54]. While historical profit metrics over multi-year windows look severe, focusing solely on the past ignores the sharp inflection happening right now, evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth of 419% and TTM sales growth of 20% [E17, E21]. The bear highlights a thin margin of safety, yet a reverse DCF proves that today's price actually prices in -0.4% earnings growth, meaning expectations are heavily depressed despite strong operational momentum [E46, E47]. Operating margins are expanding dramatically, jumping by 9 percentage points in the TTM period and reaching 17% in September 2026 compared to just 4% a year prior [E30, E31]. Balance sheet health directly counters concerns of fundamental distress, showing conservative financing with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21x and borrowings dropping to Rs 312 Cr in September 2026 [E37, E39]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is largely complete as seen in a -79.8% drop in CWIP, signaling that new capacity is ready to capture demand and validate the positive institutional money flow [E40, E44].

The bull’s reliance on TTM growth [E17, E21] ignores the reality that long-term compounded profit growth remains deeply negative at -28% over ten years and -78% over three years [E18, E20]. While the bull points to margin expansion [E30, E31], the company’s own filings describe the operating-margin trend as inconsistent over both the last two years and the last two quarters [E32, E33]. Conceded: [E37, E39, E40]. Although the bull claims the reverse DCF implies depressed expectations [E47], this must be weighed against the fact that the stock is trading at 97% of its 52-week range and is only 1.2% away from its high [E48, E49], suggesting that the market has already priced in this recent momentum. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding institutional flow [E44] is contradicted by the actual holdings data, which shows a decrease in both foreign and domestic institutional ownership since December 2023 [E42, E43]. Finally, the reliance on TTM figures masks the underlying weakness in return on equity, which has a median of 0% over the last year and only 4% over the last three years [E28, E29], rendering the current valuation risky despite the recent surge in profit [E56].
